artist: Gerry Mulligan and the Concert Jazz Band
label: Verve Records
rationale: The definitive document of Mulligan's Concert Jazz Band, and the record that answers the question his pianoless quartet had left open: whether a Mulligan-led ensemble could swing a full book. AllMusic calls it 'the definitive one' of the band's 1960s recordings and 'essential' (five stars, quoted in the Wikipedia reception table, S1); contemporaneous DownBeat also gave it five stars and praised both the recorded sound and 'superb ensemble playing and solos of consistently high quality' (S1). The band itself is the session gravity: Clark Terry, Bob Brookmeyer and Mel Lewis in the chairs, with arrangements by Mulligan, Brookmeyer and Al Cohn (as All About Jazz describes them in the same table, S1). It is a live club date rather than a studio construction — the same Village Vanguard room that carries the canon's Blakey, Rollins and Evans records — and it captures a working small-big-band of 1960 doing what the studio albums of the period could not: playing a whole set in front of an audience.

personnel_record.notes: One session: Sunday 11 December 1960 at the Village Vanguard, New York City — four sources agree on the date (S1, S3, S4 runouts, S7). The whole programme is from that session; the earlier 'Compact Jazz' CD edition (Verve 838 933-2) mixed this date with Milan and Berlin November 1960 material, and those non-Vanguard tracks are NOT part of this album. Production credits: the original Verve session engineer is uncredited in every source consulted (S2's Credits tab lists only the reissue producer Bryan Koniarz and Nat Hentoff's liner notes). The producer is recorded as Creed Taylor with epistemic 'inf', not 'obs' — Taylor was Verve's head of production from 1960, but no source in this pass prints a producer credit for this specific date, so this is the label-period inference the contract allows (the Van Gelder precedent), and the engineer is a deliberate null. Track durations follow the original six-track LP (S1, S2 40:51 total). Sides from the US mono LP label matrices (S4): A = 51,112, B = 51,113. Personnel disagreements preserved: 'Alan Raph' vs the sleeve's 'Alan Ralph' (same musician, see name_variants); Bob Brookmeyer's instrument is valve trombone, recorded as trombone per the taxonomy.

ballot.album: Gerry Mulligan and the Concert Jazz Band — At the Village Vanguard (1960)
ballot.case_for: This is a compelling defining statement of Mulligan's Concert Jazz Band: AllMusic calls it the band's 'definitive' 1960s recording and 'essential,' while contemporaneous DownBeat awarded five stars for its ensemble playing and solos (quoted in S1). Its thirteen-piece ensemble scales Mulligan's predominantly pianoless, contrapuntal approach into orchestral jazz, with Clark Terry, Bob Brookmeyer, Mel Lewis and Bill Crow providing exceptional session gravity (S3–S4). The six-track live program offers an accessible discovery route into post-bebop large-ensemble music, with Brookmeyer and Lewis also connecting this band to the later Village Vanguard orchestral tradition.
ballot.case_against: Being definitive for this ensemble does not establish jazz-wide indispensability: the dossier demonstrates strong reviews more clearly than recurring core-list status, and supplies little direct evidence of this particular album's downstream influence. Its achievement is chiefly the orchestral refinement of Mulligan's established language, making the load-bearing claim less secure than the performance-quality claim. Nearly all critical reception is mediated through Wikipedia's table rather than directly verified reviews (S1), while the personnel record still needs an explicit track-specific piano credit for Mulligan on 'Let My People Be' (S3–S4).
ballot.recommendation: The council proposes John give this strong candidate a focused listen, with direct verification of the principal reviews and correction of Mulligan's piano credit before any final decision.
